drhp.business: ACGL manufactures all types of bus variants - LCV, ICV, MCV, HCV, sleeper coaches, mobile vans, ambulances and defense vehicles - through an in-house design team, own manufacturing facilities and a strong vendor base. It also runs a capital-intensive sheet-metal Pressing segment that supplies OEMs and follows their business cyclicality. During the year the Company raised its installed manufacturing capacity to 1,200 buses per month, with a higher share of bus bodies built on the MCV platform for State Transport Undertakings (STUs).

risks.note: Company flags risk related to capability constraints with respect to the migration of ICE to EV bus bodies, evolving sustainability requirements, and capacity constraints to meet peak and future demand effectively.
Delays in digital transformation and infrastructure modernization could impact productivity, competitiveness, and progress toward environmental commitments.
risks.risk: Digital transformation and infrastructure modernization delays

risks.note: Growing presence of multinational players in the electric vehicle space, coupled with increasing collaborations between local bus body builders and foreign partners, poses competitive pressure on domestic OEMs particularly in the rapidly emerging electric bus segment.
risks.risk: Rising competitive intensity in the electric bus segment

risks.note: The prevailing geopolitical environment may impact bus exports to the Middle East and lead to an increase in commodity prices; of the 9,328 buses sold in FY26, 3,382 units were exported, indicating meaningful export exposure.
risks.risk: Geopolitical exposure on exports and input costs

risks.note: The Bus segment's revenue share clocked 92% of total company revenue during the year, making performance highly dependent on demand and pricing in that single segment.

The sheet-metal Pressing business follows the cyclicity of OEM business for which the Company is a key supplier; the segment is capital intensive and capacity utilization drives its profitability, exposing it to swings in OEM order volumes.
risks.risk: Cyclicality and OEM-dependence in the Pressing segment
